Base directory for this skill: D:\Claude-MAX-7e1ff64d\local-agent-mode-sessions\skills-plugin\dd2c3869-9069-4988-a73b-1a34acf1fcbe\514542e3-4291-4884-ba55-b10d28ac67fa\skills\xlsx

# XLSX creation, editing, and analysis

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** or **edit** with formulas/formatting | `openpyxl` — see gotchas below |
| **Bulk data** in or out | `pandas` (`read_excel`, `to_excel`) |
| **Quick look** at a sheet | `markitdown file.xlsx` — `## SheetName` per sheet; reads `.xlsm` too. No cell coordinates, so don't plan edits from it |
| **Read** a model (formulas *and* values) | two `load_workbook` passes — see gotchas |

> `openpyxl`, `pandas`, and `markitdown` are preinstalled — do not run `pip install` first; write the script and import directly. Only if an import fails (or the `markitdown` command is missing): `pip install` the missing package.

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Requirements for every output

- **Professional font** (Arial, Times New Roman) throughout, unless the user says otherwise.
- **Zero formula errors.** Never ship while `recalc.py` reports `errors_found`. If you think an error predates you, prove it: load the *original* with `data_only=True` and look at that cell. An error you introduced looks exactly like one you inherited.
- **Use formulas, never hardcoded results.** Write `sheet['B10'] = '=SUM(B2:B9)'`, not the Python-computed total. The sheet must recalculate when its inputs change.
- **Follow the user's spec literally.** Exact tab names, exact column headers, and the formula they spelled out. A redesign that computes something else fails, however elegant.
- **Document every assumption and hardcoded number** where the reader will see it — a cell comment, or an adjacent cell at a table's end. Cite a real source when one exists (`Source: Company 10-K, FY2024, Page 45, Revenue Note, [SEC EDGAR URL]`); when the number came from the user, say so plainly.
- **A workbook *you create* for someone to fill in** needs a short legend naming which cells to edit, and one example row of realistic values showing the expected format. Never add such a row to a file you were asked to edit.
- **Editing an existing file: match its conventions exactly.** They override every guideline here. Find its designated input cells first — a distinct font color, fill, or shading marks them — write only there, and leave every existing formula untouched.

## Recalculate (mandatory whenever the file contains formulas)

openpyxl writes formulas as strings with **no cached values**. Until you recalculate, every
formula cell reads back as `None` to anything reading cached values — `pandas`,
`load_workbook(data_only=True)`, and most previewers.

```bash
python scripts/recalc.py output.xlsx [timeout_seconds]   # default 30
```

LibreOffice computes every formula, the file is **rewritten in place**, and you get JSON:
`status` (`success` | `errors_found`), `total_formulas`, `total_errors`, and an
`error_summary` naming up to 100 cells per error type (`locations_truncated` says how many it
withheld — trust `total_errors`, not the length of the list). Fix what it names and run it
again. **JSON with an `error` key instead of a `status` means nothing was recalculated**, and
only that case exits non-zero — `errors_found` exits 0, so never treat a clean exit as a clean
workbook.

**A green recalc proves your formulas *evaluate*, not that they are *right*.** An off-by-one
range or a reference to the wrong row yields a clean, error-free file with wrong numbers.
Write 2–3 formulas first and check they pull the values you expect, before building out a grid.

**A workbook that links to another file loses those links** if you re-save it with openpyxl and
then recalculate. Such a formula reads `='[1]Returns Analysis'!$Bstartup` — the `[1]` is an index
into the workbook's external-reference list, naming a *separate file on disk*, not a sheet.
That file is rarely present here, so the cell's cached value is the only thing holding its
data. openpyxl strips that value on save; LibreOffice then has to resolve the reference for
real, fails, writes `#NAME?`, and deletes every link. `recalc.py` refuses to run in that state
— copy those cells' values out of the original before you save over them (`--force` overrides,
and accepts the loss).

## Choosing formulas that survive verification

LibreOffice implements fewer functions than Excel, and one it cannot evaluate becomes a
literal `#NAME?` baked into the file you deliver.

- **Prefer Excel-2007-era functions** — `SUMIFS`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `IFERROR`, `SUMPRODUCT` — which need no prefix.
- **Six post-2007 functions work, but only with an `_xlfn.` prefix**, because openpyxl writes your formula into the XML verbatim and Excel stores post-2007 names prefixed (its UI hides the prefix): `_xlfn.TEXTJOIN`, `_xlfn.CONCAT`, `_xlfn.IFS`, `_xlfn.SWITCH`, `_xlfn.MAXIFS`, `_xlfn.MINIFS`. Written bare, each yields `#NAME?`.
- **Never use `XLOOKUP`, `XMATCH`, `SORT`, `FILTER`, `UNIQUE`, or `SEQUENCE`.** The runtime's LibreOffice cannot evaluate them under *any* prefix. Newer builds do evaluate them, but they are spilling array functions and an openpyxl-written file has no spill metadata, so only the top-left cell of the range gets a value — and `recalc.py` reports `total_errors: 0` on the truncated result. Use `INDEX`/`MATCH` for lookups, and sort, filter, and de-duplicate in Python before writing the cells.
- A formula LibreOffice could not parse is written back **lowercased** — a quick tell beside a `#NAME?`.

## openpyxl gotchas

- **Reading a model takes two loads.** `data_only=True` yields cached values with the formulas gone; the default yields formula strings with no values. One pass cannot give you both.
- **`data_only=True` is destructive if you save.** That workbook has no formulas left, so saving replaces every one with a literal — permanently.
- **`data_only=True` on a file openpyxl just wrote returns `None` everywhere** — run `recalc.py` first. (A formula whose result is `""` also reads back as `None`.)
- **Merged cells: write the top-left anchor only.** Every other cell in the range is a `MergedCell` whose `.value` is read-only.
- **`.xlsm` loses its macros unless you pass `keep_vba=True`** to `load_workbook`.
- **A sheet name containing a space must be quoted** in a cross-sheet reference: `='Assumptions Inputs'!$Bworkbook`. Unquoted, it evaluates to `#VALUE!`.

## Financial models

Unless the user says otherwise, or the existing file already does something else.

**Color:** blue text (`0,0,255`) for hardcoded inputs and scenario levers · black for formulas ·
green (`0,128,0`) for links to another sheet · red (`255,0,0`) for links to another file ·
yellow fill (`255,255,0`) for key assumptions and cells the user should fill in.

**Numbers:** currency `$#,##0`, with the unit named in the header (`Revenue ($mm)`) · zeros
render as `-`, including in percentages (`$#,##0;($#,##0);-`) · negatives in parentheses ·
percentages `0.0%`, **stored as fractions** (`0.15` renders `15.0%`; storing `15` renders
`1500.0%`) · valuation multiples `0.0x` · years as text (`"2024"`, never `2,024`).

**Structure:** every assumption in its own labeled cell, referenced by the formulas that use it
(`=B5*(1+$Bfor)`, never `=B5*1.05`) · formulas consistent across every projection period, since a
lone edited cell mid-row is the commonest silent error · guard denominators that can be zero.

## Dependencies

`openpyxl`, `pandas`, `markitdown` (pip, preinstalled — install only if an import fails or the command is missing) · LibreOffice (`soffice`, auto-configured for sandboxed environments via `scripts/office/soffice.py`)

"""Build results/business_model.xlsx: the trading-swarm business model for import into cfo.ai.

Every number the model uses is an input on the Assumptions sheet; every other cell is a formula.
"""
import sys

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.comments import Comment
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, PatternFill, Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter

OUT = sys.argv[1]
MONTHS = 24
FIRST_COL = 3                      # month 1 in column C
LAST = get_column_letter(FIRST_COL + MONTHS - 1)

FONT = "Arial"
BLUE, BLACK, GREEN = "0000FF", "000000", "008000"
YELLOW = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFFF00")
HEADER_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="D9E1F2")
THIN = Border(bottom=Side(style="thin", color="999999"))
USD = '$#,##0;($#,##0);"-"'
USD_CENTS = '$#,##0.00;($#,##0.00);"-"'
USD_MILLS = '$0.000;($0.000);"-"'
PCT = '0.0%;(0.0%);"-"'
COUNT = '#,##0.0;(#,##0.0);"-"'
INT = '#,##0;(#,##0);"-"'


def font(color=BLACK, bold=False, size=10, italic=False):
    return Font(name=FONT, color=color, bold=bold, size=size, italic=italic)


def style_all(ws):
    for row in ws.iter_rows():
        for c in row:
            if c.font.name != FONT:
                c.font = Font(name=FONT, size=c.font.size or 10, bold=c.font.bold,
                              italic=c.font.italic, color=c.font.color)


wb = Workbook()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Assumptions
A = wb.active
A.title = "Assumptions"
A["A1"] = "Trading swarm: business model assumptions"
A["A1"].font = font(bold=True, size=13)
A["A2"] = ("Legend: blue = input you can change. Yellow = key assumption to confirm (owner's estimate, "
           "not measured). Black = formula. Green = link to another sheet. Column B feeds Model_Base, "
           "column C feeds Model_Growth.")
A["A2"].font = font(italic=True, size=9)
A["A3"] = ("Product: a pre-trade gate for paper and retail algo traders. For each watchlist ticker, every "
           "trading day, a four-agent swarm decides whether a +5%/-3%/10-day trade has evidence behind it, "
           "and refuses when it doesn't. Priced per watchlist (5 tickers) per month.")
A["A3"].font = font(size=9)
A["A3"].alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="top")
A.merge_cells("A3:E3")
A.row_dimensions[3].height = 40

headers = ["Assumption", "Base", "Growth", "Unit", "Source or note"]
for i, h in enumerate(headers, 1):
    c = A.cell(row=5, column=i, value=h)
    c.font = font(bold=True)
    c.fill = HEADER_FILL
    c.border = THIN

# key, label, base, growth, unit, number format, key assumption?, source
ROWS = [
    ("price", "Price per watchlist per month", 19, 19, "$ / month", USD_CENTS, True,
     "Owner assumption: a hobbyist-tier subscription price. Not tested with customers."),
    ("tickers", "Tickers per watchlist", 5, 5, "tickers", INT, False,
     "Matches the project's 5-ticker watchlist (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA)."),
    ("days", "Trading days per month", 21, 21, "days", INT, False,
     "About 252 US trading days a year / 12."),
    ("decisions", "Decisions per watchlist per month", "=B7*B8", "=C7*C8", "decisions", INT, False,
     "Formula: tickers x trading days. One swarm decision per ticker per day."),
    ("llm", "LLM cost per decision", 0.038, 0.038, "$ / decision", USD_MILLS, False,
     "Measured: $11.76 logged over 310 validation setups on 2026-10-10 (results/README.md). Upper bound: "
     "DeepSeek peak, cache-miss prices. Off-peak rates are half (about $0.019)."),
    ("laya", "Laya inference cost per decision", 0, 0, "$ / decision", USD_MILLS, False,
     "Laya is a local classifier (about 33 ms per question on a T4 GPU). Marginal cost about zero; "
     "set above zero if it runs on paid GPUs. Not used in production unless the step 9 go/no-go passes."),
    ("fee_pct", "Payment fee, share of price", 0.029, 0.029, "%", PCT, False,
     "Stripe standard US card pricing: 2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge."),
    ("fee_fixed", "Payment fee, fixed per charge", 0.30, 0.30, "$ / charge", USD_CENTS, False,
     "Stripe standard US card pricing."),
    ("start_customers", "Customers at start", 0, 0, "customers", INT, False, "Pre-launch."),
    ("new1", "New customers in month 1", 10, 25, "customers", INT, True,
     "Owner assumption. Base: organic from build-in-public posts. Growth: plus paid acquisition."),
    ("new_growth", "Monthly growth in new customers", 0.05, 0.10, "% / month", PCT, True,
     "Owner assumption."),
    ("churn", "Monthly churn", 0.08, 0.06, "% / month", PCT, True,

    ("team", "Team cost per month", 2000, 6000, "$ / month", USD, True,

    for col, val in ((2, base), (3, growth)):

    A.column_dimensions[col].width = width

    return "Assumptions!$%s$%d" % (col, REF[key])

MODEL_ROWS = {}     # label key -> row number on model sheets


def build_model(title, col):
    ws = wb.create_sheet(title)
    ws["A1"] = "%s scenario: monthly model (months 1-%d)" % (title.split("_")[1], MONTHS)

    for line in lines:

U.column_dimensions["A"].width = 42
for col in "BC":

U.column_dimensions["D"].width = 14

S["A1"].font = font(bold=True, size=13)

MONTHS = 24

HEADER_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="D9E1F2")

def font(color=BLACK, bold=False, size=10, italic=False):
    return Font(name=FONT, color=color, bold=bold, size=size, italic=italic)


def style_all(ws):
    for row in ws.iter_rows():
        for c in row:
            if c.font.name != FONT:
                c.font = Font(name=FONT, size=c.font.size or 10, bold=c.font.bold,
                              italic=c.font.italic, color=c.font.color)


wb = Workbook()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Assumptions
A = wb.active
A.title = "Assumptions"
A["A1"] = "Trading swarm: business model assumptions"
A["A1"].font = font(bold=True, size=13)
A["A2"] = ("Legend: blue = input you can change. Yellow = key assumption to confirm (owner's estimate, "
           "not measured). Black = formula. Green = link to another sheet. Column B feeds Model_Base, "
           "column C feeds Model_Growth.")
A["A2"].font = font(italic=True, size=9)
A["A3"] = ("Product: a pre-trade gate for paper and retail algo traders. For each watchlist ticker, every "
           "trading day, a four-agent swarm decides whether a +5%/-3%/10-day trade has evidence behind it, "
           "and refuses when it doesn't. Priced per watchlist (5 tickers) per month.")
A["A3"].font = font(size=9)
A["A3"].alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="top")
A.merge_cells("A3:E3")
A.row_dimensions[3].height = 40

headers = ["Assumption", "Base", "Growth", "Unit", "Source or note"]
for i, h in enumerate(headers, 1):
    c = A.cell(row=5, column=i, value=h)
    c.font = font(bold=True)
    c.fill = HEADER_FILL
    c.border = THIN

# key, label, base, growth, unit, number format, key assumption?, source
ROWS = [
    ("price", "Price per watchlist per month", 19, 19, "$ / month", USD_CENTS, True,
     "Owner assumption: a hobbyist-tier subscription price. Not tested with customers."),
    ("tickers", "Tickers per watchlist", 5, 5, "tickers", INT, False,
     "Matches the project's 5-ticker watchlist (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA)."),
    ("days", "Trading days per month", 21, 21, "days", INT, False,
     "About 252 US trading days a year / 12."),
    ("decisions", "Decisions per watchlist per month", "=B7*B8", "=C7*C8", "decisions", INT, False,
     "Formula: tickers x trading days. One swarm decision per ticker per day."),
    ("llm", "LLM cost per decision", 0.038, 0.038, "$ / decision", USD_MILLS, False,
     "Measured: $11.76 logged over 310 validation setups on 2026-10-10 (results/README.md). Upper bound: "
     "DeepSeek peak, cache-miss prices. Off-peak rates are half (about $0.019)."),
    ("laya", "Laya inference cost per decision", 0, 0, "$ / decision", USD_MILLS, False,
     "Laya is a local classifier (about 33 ms per question on a T4 GPU). Marginal cost about zero; "
     "set above zero if it runs on paid GPUs. Not used in production unless the step 9 go/no-go passes."),
    ("fee_pct", "Payment fee, share of price", 0.029, 0.029, "%", PCT, False,
     "Stripe standard US card pricing: 2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge."),
    ("fee_fixed", "Payment fee, fixed per charge", 0.30, 0.30, "$ / charge", USD_CENTS, False,
     "Stripe standard US card pricing."),
    ("start_customers", "Customers at start", 0, 0, "customers", INT, False, "Pre-launch."),
    ("new1", "New customers in month 1", 10, 25, "customers", INT, True,
     "Owner assumption. Base: organic from build-in-public posts. Growth: plus paid acquisition."),
    ("new_growth", "Monthly growth in new customers", 0.05, 0.10, "% / month", PCT, True,
     "Owner assumption."),
    ("churn", "Monthly churn", 0.08, 0.06, "% / month", PCT, True,

        None,
        ("cust_start", "Customers, start of month", "customers", "=" + a("start_customers", col), "={p}{r_cust_end}", COUNT, None),
        ("new", "New customers", "customers",
         "=%s*(1+%s)^({c}{r_month}-1)" % (a("new1", col), a("new_growth", col)), None, COUNT, BLACK),
        ("churned", "Churned customers", "customers", "={c}{r_cust_start}*%s" % a("churn", col), None, COUNT, BLACK),
        ("cust_end", "Customers, end of month", "customers", "={c}{r_cust_start}+{c}{r_new}-{c}{r_churned}", None, COUNT, BLACK),
        None,
        ("revenue", "Revenue (MRR)", "$", "={c}{r_cust_end}*%s" % a("price", col), None, USD, BLACK),
        ("fees", "Payment fees", "$", "={c}{r_cust_end}*(%s*%s+%s)" % (a("price", col), a("fee_pct", col), a("fee_fixed", col)), None, USD, BLACK),
        ("llm", "LLM inference", "$", "={c}{r_cust_end}*%s*%s" % (a("decisions", col), a("llm", col)), None, USD, BLACK),
        ("laya", "Laya inference", "$", "={c}{r_cust_end}*%s*%s" % (a("decisions", col), a("laya", col)), None, USD, BLACK),
        ("gross", "Gross profit", "$", "={c}{r_revenue}-{c}{r_fees}-{c}{r_llm}-{c}{r_laya}", None, USD, BLACK),
        ("gm", "Gross margin", "%", "=IF({c}{r_revenue}=0,0,{c}{r_gross}/{c}{r_revenue})", None, PCT, BLACK),

        ("cash_end", "Cash, end of month", "$", "={c}{r_cash_start}+{c}{r_op}", None, USD, BLACK),
        None,
        ("flag_cash", "Flag: cash below zero (1 = yes)", "flag", "=IF({c}{r_cash_end}<0,1,0)", None, INT, BLACK),

        ws.cell(row=rr, column=2, value=unit).font = font(size=9)

            cell = ws.cell(row=rr, column=colno, value=int(value) if value.isdigit() else value)
            cell.number_format = fmt
            if key == "month":
                cell.font = font(BLUE if m == 0 else BLACK, bold=True)
                cell.fill = HEADER_FILL
            else:
                link = value.startswith("=Assumptions!") or (color is None and m == 0)

    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 44

"""Evaluate every formula with pycel, then check key outputs against an independent Python model."""
import math, sys
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from pycel import ExcelCompiler

path = sys.argv[1]
wb = load_workbook(path)
xl = ExcelCompiler(filename=path)

errors, count = [], 0
for ws in wb.worksheets:
    for row in ws.iter_rows():
        for c in row:
            if isinstance(c.value, str) and c.value.startswith("="):
                count += 1
                v = xl.evaluate("%s!%s" % (ws.title, c.coordinate))
                if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("#"):
                    errors.append((ws.title, c.coordinate, v, c.value))
print("formulas evaluated:", count, "| errors:", len(errors))
for e in errors[:10]: print("  ", e)

def model(price, tickers, days, llm, laya, fee_pct, fee_fixed, start, new1, g, churn, cac, hosting, neat, team, cash0):
    cust, cash, out = start, cash0, {"cash": [], "op": [], "cust": [], "rev": []}
    for m in range(1, 25):
        new = new1 * (1 + g) ** (m - 1)
        end = cust + new - cust * churn
        rev = end * price
        gross = rev - end * (price * fee_pct + fee_fixed) - end * tickers * days * (llm + laya)
        op = gross - new * cac - hosting - neat - team
        cash += op
        for k, v in (("cash", cash), ("op", op), ("cust", end), ("rev", rev)): out[k].append(v)
        cust = end
    return out

S = {"Base": model(19, 5, 21, 0.038, 0, 0.029, 0.30, 0, 10, 0.05, 0.08, 30, 100, 0, 2000, 25000),
     "Growth": model(19, 5, 21, 0.038, 0, 0.029, 0.30, 0, 25, 0.10, 0.06, 40, 100, 0, 6000, 25000)}
checks = []
for col, name in (("B", "Base"), ("C", "Growth")):
    o = S[name]
    first_neg = next((i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(o["cash"]) if v < 0), "none within 24 months")
    first_profit = next((i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(o["op"]) if v >= 0), "not within 24 months")
    expect = {5: o["cust"][11], 6: o["cust"][23], 7: o["rev"][11], 8: o["rev"][23], 11: sum(o["op"]),
              12: min(o["cash"]), 13: o["cash"][23], 14: first_neg, 15: first_profit, 16: max(0, -min(o["cash"]))}
    for row, want in expect.items():
        got = xl.evaluate("Summary!%s%d" % (col, row))
        ok = (got == want) if isinstance(want, str) else math.isclose(float(got), want, rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-6)
        checks.append(ok)
        print("%-7s Summary!%s%-3d %-28s sheet=%s python=%s %s" % (name, col, row, wb["Summary"].cell(row=row, column=1).value[:28],
              round(got, 2) if not isinstance(got, str) else got, round(want, 2) if not isinstance(want, str) else want, "OK" if ok else "MISMATCH"))
cm = 19 - (19 * 0.029 + 0.30) - 105 * 0.038
for col, churn, cac in (("B", 0.08, 30), ("C", 0.06, 40)):
    for row, want in ((8, cm), (12, cm / churn), (13, cm / churn / cac)):
        got = xl.evaluate("Unit_Economics!%s%d" % (col, row))
        ok = math.isclose(got, want, rel_tol=1e-9); checks.append(ok)
        print("Unit_Economics!%s%d sheet=%.3f python=%.3f %s" % (col, row, got, want, "OK" if ok else "MISMATCH"))
print("ALL CHECKS PASS" if all(checks) and not errors else "CHECKS FAILED")

# Building the business plan in cfo.ai

The model is ready as an Excel workbook: `results/business_model.xlsx`. cfo.ai's assistant, Ari, can import a workbook and rebuild it as a native cfo.ai model, turning the assumptions into Variables and the two cases into Scenarios (cfo.ai docs: "Import a spreadsheet model").

## What's in the workbook

| Sheet | Contents |
|---|---|
| Summary | 24-month results for both scenarios: customers, MRR, gross margin, operating profit, lowest cash, runway, break-even, funding need, LTV:CAC |
| Assumptions | Every input with its source. Blue = input, yellow = owner estimate to confirm. Column B = Base, column C = Growth |
| Model_Base, Model_Growth | Monthly model: customers, revenue, payment fees, LLM and Laya cost, gross profit, marketing, fixed costs, operating profit, cash |
| Unit_Economics | One watchlist per month: contribution margin, CAC payback, LTV, LTV:CAC |

Every output is a formula; there are no typed-in results. All 1,010 formulas were evaluated (with pycel) and checked against an independent Python calculation of the same model; they match. The file has no cached values, because it was written by a script: Excel computes them when it opens the file, and Ari reads the formulas.

## Measured vs assumed

- **Measured:** LLM cost per decision, $0.038 (upper bound at DeepSeek peak prices, from the validation run in `results/README.md`).
- **Standard pricing:** card fees, 2.9% + $0.30 (Stripe US).
- **Owner estimates (yellow):** price ($19 per watchlist per month), new customers, growth, churn, CAC, hosting, neatlogs, team cost, starting cash. Change them before presenting the plan if you have better numbers.

## Results with the current assumptions

| | Base | Growth |
|---|---|---|
| Customers, month 24 | 238 | 1,504 |
| MRR, month 24 | $4,516 | $28,569 |
| Contribution margin per watchlist | $14.16 (74.5%) | $14.16 (74.5%) |
| LTV to CAC | 5.9x | 5.9x |
| Break-even month | 22 | 18 |
| Lowest cash balance | $682 | −$43,130 |
| Funding needed to never go below zero | $0 | $43,130 |

Reading: unit economics are healthy because inference is cheap per decision. Base survives on $25,000 but only just. Growth needs about $43,000 of outside funding before it breaks even in month 18.

## Steps (Zeeshan)

1. Sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks. **Cancel the subscription immediately** in Settings → Billing, as the hackathon page instructs. The neatHack team provides credits.
2. Optional: open `results/business_model.xlsx` in Excel, change any yellow assumption, and save. Saving in Excel also stores the computed values.
3. Start a conversation with Ari, attach the workbook, and paste:

   > Import this workbook into cfo.ai as a native Model. It is a 24-month plan for a subscription product priced per watchlist. Make every input on the Assumptions sheet a Variable. Make column B (Base) the Main scenario and column C (Growth) a second Scenario. Keep the monthly time grain starting at month 1, with no Actuals.

4. Check the rebuild, paste:

   > Reconcile the rebuilt revenue, gross profit, operating profit and ending cash to the attached workbook for months 12 and 24 in both scenarios, and list any differences.

5. Ask Ari for the runway view and a short plan summary:

   > Show runway and the funding needed for each scenario, and draft a one-page business plan summary from this Model.

6. Share the model or page as a read-only link and put the link, plus a screenshot, in the submission. Save a PDF or screenshots to `results/` too.

**Done when:** the Model has both Scenarios, the reconciliation shows no differences, and the share link is in the submission.

# What to do next

Written 2026-10-11 after the step 5 validation run. Work through the sections in order. Owners are suggestions: Elena has the Kaggle setup for Laya; Zeeshan has the DeepSeek, neatlogs and cfo.ai accounts.

## Where we stand

| Done | Where |
|---|---|
| Steps 1–4: data, labels, splits, Laya export and fine-tune, baselines | `step-1-4` branch, `docs/HANDOVER.md` |
| Step 5: four-agent swarm, neatlogs tracing, paper-trade simulator | `swarm` branch, `src/` |
| Step 6 (swarm part): full validation run, 577 setups, 0 errors | `swarm` branch, `results/` |

**Validation result:** the swarm approved 1 of 577 setups (it lost 3%). Approving everything gives 36.6% precision, below the 37.5% break-even, and the baselines found no signal in the price features. Honest claim: *the swarm refuses to trade a market with no edge*. It does not show the swarm picks winners.

## Gaps against the judging criteria

| Criterion | Weight | Status | Fix in section |
|---|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | Works end to end on real data; result is "refuses to trade" | 3, 5 |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | neatlogs done. **Entire and cfo.ai not started** | 2, 4 |
| Demo video | 20% | Not started | 6 |
| Building in public | 15% | Nothing posted yet | 7 |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | Story in section 6 | 6 |

The biggest cheap win is Entire and cfo.ai: 25% of the score, no model runs needed.

## 1. Housekeeping (Zeeshan, 15 min)

1. **Rotate the neatlogs API key.** The old SDK printed it in a run log, so treat it as exposed. Put the new one in `.env`.
2. **Delete `.env.txt` and `New Text Document.txt`** from the repo folder. `.env.txt` holds a key (it is gitignored, but should not exist).
3. **Merge PR #3** (swarm spec review) into `main`.
4. **Open a PR from `swarm` into `main`.** `docs/SWARM_SPEC.md` will differ from PR #3 in two places: the DeepSeek model table (section 3) and the leakage note (section 6). Keep both.

**Done when:** PR #3 is merged, the `swarm` PR is open, and `git status` shows no stray files.

## 2. Entire (Zeeshan, 30–45 min)

Entire records the context behind each AI-made change (prompt, transcript, tool calls, files) as a checkpoint linked to the commit. The hackathon wants it used to *build and improve* the agent, so every change from here on should go through it. Docs: https://docs.entire.io

1. Install (Windows PowerShell):
   ```powershell
   irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
   ```
   Check with `entire version`.
2. In the repo root, enable it for Claude Code:
   ```bash
   entire enable -y --agent claude-code
   ```
3. Add the code graph (local only, no network):
   ```bash
   entire plugin install graph
   ```
   ```bash
   entire graph init-agents --repo .
   ```
   `init-agents` adds managed blocks to `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Review the diff before committing.
4. Make the next real change with Claude Code (section 5's test-run flag is a good first one), commit it, and answer `y` when Entire asks to link the commit to the session.
5. Check it: `entire checkpoint list`.

**Done when:** at least one commit on the branch has an Entire checkpoint. For the demo, pick a checkpoint where you can show the prompt and the resulting change side by side.

## 3. Laya validation scores and the go/no-go (Elena, 30–60 min)

This is the step `docs/HANDOVER.md` lists as next. Use Route A (Kaggle notebook) from the handover; it has the commands.

**Decision rule, written before the run:**
- If fine-tuned Laya's validation AUC has a 90% interval whose lower end is above 0.5, try the ensemble: per `docs/SWARM_SPEC.md` section 7, Laya's calibrated probability replaces `hit_rate_low` as p in the gate. Add that as a new spec section before coding it.

content.text:
Almost all the cost is the Planner, so that's where the savings are. From the validation run's decision log:

| Agent | Model | Calls (577 setups) |
|---|---|---|
| Researcher | `deepseek-flash`, thinking off | 577 |
| **Planner** | **`deepseek-v4-pro`, thinking on, high effort** | **1,154** (every setup used both rounds) |
| Naysayer | `deepseek-v4-pro`, thinking on | ~26 (the code gate blocks most plans before it's called) |

The Planner makes two-thirds of the calls, on the expensive model, with long thinking output. It's probably 90% or more of the $0.038 per setup. That's an estimate; neatlogs can confirm it, since every LLM span has its token counts.

**Options, cheapest wins first:**

1. **Run off-peak (no code change).** DeepSeek charges half price outside 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC on weekdays. Our run (18:12–19:59 UTC) was already off-peak, so real spend is probably about half the logged figure, around $0.019 per setup. The logger always uses peak prices; a small fix would log the real rate. Your DeepSeek dashboard has the exact number.
2. **Pre-check the gate in code before calling the Planner (biggest saving).** 576 of 577 setups were refused. Code can check train data for simple 1–2-condition theses that today's setup meets. If none can pass the gate, refuse with no LLM call at all. Likely saving: 70–90%. Train data can tell us the exact share for free. Caveats: it's a spec change, and testing many conditions makes chance "evidence" more likely. So it should only decide when to *skip*; the Planner still has to pass the gate on its own.
3. **Lower the Planner's thinking effort,** high → low, or thinking off. Thinking tokens are most of the output, so roughly 2–4× cheaper per call. The trade-off is plan quality.
4. **Use `deepseek-flash` for the Planner:** about 3–4× cheaper per token, same quality question.
5. **Make round 2 conditional.** Round 2 succeeded once in 577 setups, which was the only approval. Dropping it halves Planner calls. A middle ground: retry only for fixable failures (too few matches, invalid plan), not for a hit rate far below break-even.
6. **Have code write the Researcher's facts.** A small saving, around 3%, plus one fewer moving part.
7. **Product level: decide only on real price moves, not every ticker every day.** This was the original watcher idea. Fewer decisions per watchlist directly improves the cfo.ai numbers.

**My recommendation: 1 + 2 + 3 together.** That plausibly cuts cost per decision by about 10×. Prove it with a before/after on 20 setups (`--limit 20`), comparing cost and decisions in neatlogs. That's also the hackathon's "use neatlogs to improve the agent" story. Make the change under Entire, so it's checkpointed, and update the LLM cost cell in the cfo.ai workbook afterwards.

Changes 2–5 alter decisions, so they belong before the one-shot test run. The validation run would need a re-run, which becomes cheap once these are in.

Which ones should I implement?

Done in this order: measure first (free, uses only train data and validation features, no LLM calls), then code, tests, and a spec section. One problem up front, with option 3:

**DeepSeek has no "medium" effort.** Its docs list `low`, `high`, and `max`, and say `medium` is treated as `high`. So "medium" would cost exactly what we pay now. I'll do 7, 5, and 2, leave the Planner at `high` for now, and ask you about `low` at the end.

First, measuring how often the price watcher would fire, and how often the pre-check would let us skip the LLM:

input.command:
cd "D:/user/projects/trading-swarm" && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, itertools, math
from src.tools import load_market, wilson_low
from src.features import FEATURE_NAMES
m = load_market()
s = m.setups
z = (s.ret_1d.abs() / s.vol_20d)
for k in (1.0, 1.5, 2.0):
    print("watcher |ret_1d| >= %.1f x vol_20d: train %.1f%%  validation %.1f%%" % (k, 100*(z[s.split=="train"] >= k).mean(), 100*(z[s.split=="validation"] >= k).mean()))

train = s[s.split == "train"].reset_index(drop=True)
qs = np.arange(0.1, 1.0, 0.1)
thr = {f: np.quantile(train[f], qs) for f in FEATURE_NAMES}
labels = train.label.to_numpy()
def precheck(row, use_pairs):
    known = (train.outcome_end < pd.Timestamp(row.date)).to_numpy()
    elig = known.sum()
    cands = []
    for f in FEATURE_NAMES:
        for t in thr[f]:
            mask = (train[f] >= t).to_numpy() if row[f] >= t else (train[f] <= t).to_numpy()
            cands.append(mask & known)
    def passes(mask):
        n = mask.sum()
        if n < 30 or n > 0.8 * elig: return False
        return wilson_low(int(labels[mask].sum()), int(n)) > 0.375
    if any(passes(c) for c in cands): return True
    if use_pairs:
        for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(cands)), 2):
            if i // 9 != j // 9 and passes(cands[i] & cands[j]): return True
    return False
val = s[s.split == "validation"]
trig = val[(val.ret_1d.abs() / val.vol_20d) >= 1.5]
for use_pairs in (False, True):
    ok = [precheck(r, use_pairs) for r in trig.itertuples()]
    print("pre-check (%s) on %d triggered validation setups: passable %d, skipped %d (%.0f%%)" % ("singles+pairs" if use_pairs else "singles only", len(trig), sum(ok), len(ok)-sum(ok), 100*(1-np.mean(ok))))
EOF

"""Step 5: the four-agent swarm. One decision line per setup, then a summary.

For each setup: Researcher -> Planner -> Mathematician -> Naysayer. A block sends the
objections back to the Planner, up to MAX_ROUNDS rounds; then the setup is dropped.
Approved plans become paper trades, closed by the simulator only after the decision
is logged. Agents never see the label, the ticker, the date, or raw price levels.

    python -m src.swarm --split validation --limit 5     # smoke run
    python -m src.swarm --split validation               # baseline run
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import numpy as np

from src.agents import mathematician, naysayer, planner, researcher
from src.features import FEATURE_NAMES
from src.simulator import simulate
from src.tools import backtest, get_prices

MAX_ROUNDS = 2
LOOKBACK = 20
SUMMARY_PATH = os.path.join("runs", "swarm_summary.md")


def normalized(plan):
    """The plan as the agents see it: entry scaled to 100, no ticker."""
    scale = 100.0 / plan["entry"]
    return {"entry": 100.0, "stop": round(plan["stop"] * scale, 4),
            "target": round(plan["target"] * scale, 4), "horizon_days": plan["horizon_days"],
            "thesis": plan["thesis"], "conditions": plan["conditions"],
            "facts_cited": plan["facts_cited"]}


def decide(setup, market, llm, tracer):
    """Run the agents on one setup. Returns the decision record (no outcome yet)."""
    ticker, date = setup["ticker"], setup["date"]
    tags = {"ticker": ticker, "date": date}
    features = {k: float(setup[k]) for k in FEATURE_NAMES}
    with tracer.span("workflow", "swarm", **tags):
        with tracer.span("tool", "get_prices", agent="researcher", round=0, **tags) as rec:
            recent = get_prices(market, ticker, date, LOOKBACK)
            entry = float(recent["Adj Close"].iloc[-1])
            closes = [round(100 * c / entry, 2) for c in recent["Adj Close"]]
            rec["input"], rec["output"] = {"lookback_days": LOOKBACK}, closes
        facts = researcher.run(llm, features, closes, round=0, **tags)

        objections, plan, verdict, rnd = [], None, "block", 0
        for rnd in range(1, MAX_ROUNDS + 1):
            raw = planner.run(llm, features, facts, objections, round=rnd, **tags)
            plan, err = planner.build(raw, ticker, entry, facts, features)
            if err:
                verdict, objections = "block", ["invalid plan: " + err]
                continue
            with tracer.span("tool", "backtest", agent="mathematician", round=rnd, **tags) as rec:
                bt = backtest(plan, market, date)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = normalized(plan), bt
            with tracer.span("agent", "mathematician", agent="mathematician", round=rnd, **tags) as rec:
                math = mathematician.run(plan, bt)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = bt, math
            verdict, objections = naysayer.run(llm, normalized(plan), facts, math, round=rnd, **tags)
            if verdict == "approve":
                break
    return {"ticker": ticker, "date": date, "split": setup["split"], "rounds": rnd,
            "verdict": "approve" if verdict == "approve" else "dropped",
            "plan": plan, "objections": objections}


def run(split, market, llm, tracer, limit=None, out_path=None, workers=1, resume=False):
    """Decide every setup in `split`, simulate approved trades, write JSONL. Returns the records.

    With workers > 1, setups are decided in parallel threads; lines are still written in
    setup order. With resume, setups already in out_path without an error are kept as they

"""Step 5: the four-agent swarm. One decision line per setup, then a summary.

For each setup: Researcher -> Planner -> Mathematician -> Naysayer. A block sends the
objections back to the Planner, up to MAX_ROUNDS rounds; then the setup is dropped.
Approved plans become paper trades, closed by the simulator only after the decision
is logged. Agents never see the label, the ticker, the date, or raw price levels.

    python -m src.swarm --split validation --limit 5     # smoke run
    python -m src.swarm --split validation               # baseline run
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import numpy as np

from src.agents import mathematician, naysayer, planner, researcher
from src.features import FEATURE_NAMES
from src.simulator import simulate
from src.tools import backtest, get_prices

MAX_ROUNDS = 2
LOOKBACK = 20
SUMMARY_PATH = os.path.join("runs", "swarm_summary.md")


def normalized(plan):
    """The plan as the agents see it: entry scaled to 100, no ticker."""
    scale = 100.0 / plan["entry"]
    return {"entry": 100.0, "stop": round(plan["stop"] * scale, 4),
            "target": round(plan["target"] * scale, 4), "horizon_days": plan["horizon_days"],
            "thesis": plan["thesis"], "conditions": plan["conditions"],
            "facts_cited": plan["facts_cited"]}


def decide(setup, market, llm, tracer):
    """Run the agents on one setup. Returns the decision record (no outcome yet)."""
    ticker, date = setup["ticker"], setup["date"]
    tags = {"ticker": ticker, "date": date}
    features = {k: float(setup[k]) for k in FEATURE_NAMES}
    with tracer.span("workflow", "swarm", **tags):
        with tracer.span("tool", "get_prices", agent="researcher", round=0, **tags) as rec:
            recent = get_prices(market, ticker, date, LOOKBACK)
            entry = float(recent["Adj Close"].iloc[-1])
            closes = [round(100 * c / entry, 2) for c in recent["Adj Close"]]
            rec["input"], rec["output"] = {"lookback_days": LOOKBACK}, closes
        facts = researcher.run(llm, features, closes, round=0, **tags)

        objections, plan, verdict, rnd = [], None, "block", 0
        for rnd in range(1, MAX_ROUNDS + 1):
            raw = planner.run(llm, features, facts, objections, round=rnd, **tags)
            plan, err = planner.build(raw, ticker, entry, facts, features)
            if err:
                verdict, objections = "block", ["invalid plan: " + err]
                continue
            with tracer.span("tool", "backtest", agent="mathematician", round=rnd, **tags) as rec:
                bt = backtest(plan, market, date)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = normalized(plan), bt
            with tracer.span("agent", "mathematician", agent="mathematician", round=rnd, **tags) as rec:
                math = mathematician.run(plan, bt)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = bt, math
            verdict, objections = naysayer.run(llm, normalized(plan), facts, math, round=rnd, **tags)
            if verdict == "approve":
                break
    return {"ticker": ticker, "date": date, "split": setup["split"], "rounds": rnd,
            "verdict": "approve" if verdict == "approve" else "dropped",
            "plan": plan, "objections": objections}


def run(split, market, llm, tracer, limit=None, out_path=None, workers=1, resume=False):
    """Decide every setup in `split`, simulate approved trades, write JSONL. Returns the records.

    With workers > 1, setups are decided in parallel threads; lines are still written in
    setup order. With resume, setups already in out_path without an error are kept as they
    are and only the rest are decided. Output goes to a temp file that replaces out_path at
    the end, so an interrupted run never destroys earlier results.
    """
    if split == "test":
        raise SystemExit("The swarm step does not run on the test split.")
    rows = market.setups[market.setups["split"] == split]
    if limit:
        rows = rows.head(limit)
    out_path = out_path or os.path.join("runs", "swarm_%s.jsonl" % split)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)

    done = {}
    if resume and os.path.exists(out_path):
        with open(out_path) as f:
            for line in f:
                r = json.loads(line)
                if r["verdict"] != "error":
                    done[(r["ticker"], r["date"])] = r

    def one(setup):
        if (setup["ticker"], setup["date"]) in done:
            return done[(setup["ticker"], setup["date"])]
        try:
            rec = decide(setup, market, llm, tracer)
        except Exception as e:     # one bad setup must not stop the run; it is logged as an error
            rec = {"ticker": setup["ticker"], "date": setup["date"], "split": split,
                   "rounds": None, "verdict": "error", "plan": None, "objections": [],
                   "error": repr(e)}
        # The decision is fixed above. Only now does anything read prices after the setup date.
        if rec["verdict"] == "approve":
            rec.update(simulate(rec["plan"], market, setup["ticker"], setup["date"]))
        else:
            rec.update(trade_outcome=None, pnl_pct=None)
        rec["label"] = int(setup["label"])   # for scoring only; agents never saw it
        return rec

    records = []
    tmp_path = out_path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w") as f, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        for rec in pool.map(one, rows.to_dict("records")):   # map keeps setup order
            f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
            f.flush()
            records.append(rec)
    os.replace(tmp_path, out_path)
    return records


def summarize(records, market, split, cost=0.0, seed=0):
    """Markdown summary: swarm vs random approvals vs always-approve vs buy-and-hold."""
    labels = np.array([r["label"] for r in records])
    approved = [r for r in records if r["verdict"] == "approve"]
    n, k = len(records), len(approved)
    rate = k / n if n else 0.0
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    random_pick = rng.random(n) < rate                      # same approval rate as the swarm
    dates = market.setups.loc[market.setups["split"] == split, "date"]
    bh = [market.prices[t].loc[dates.min():dates.max(), "Adj Close"] for t in market.prices]
    bh_return = float(np.mean([s.iloc[-1] / s.iloc[0] - 1 for s in bh]))

    def pct(x):
        return "n/a" if x is None else "%.1f%%" % (100 * x)

    lines = [
        "# Swarm summary: %s split" % split, "",
        "| Item | Value |", "|---|---|",
        "| Setups | %d |" % n,
        "| Approved | %d (%s) |" % (k, pct(rate)),
        "| Dropped after %d rounds | %d |" % (MAX_ROUNDS, sum(r["verdict"] == "dropped" for r in records)),
        "| Errors | %d |" % sum(r["verdict"] == "error" for r in records),
        "| LLM cost | $%.4f |" % cost, "",
        "## Precision of approved trades (share that hit +5% before -3%)", "",
        "| Method | Approved | Precision |", "|---|---|---|",
        "| Swarm | %d | %s |" % (k, pct(np.mean([r["trade_outcome"] == "win" for r in approved]) if k else None)),
        "| Random, same approval rate (seed %d) | %d | %s |" % (seed, random_pick.sum(), pct(labels[random_pick].mean() if random_pick.any() else None)),
        "| Always approve (= base rate) | %d | %s |" % (n, pct(labels.mean() if n else None)), "",
        "Mean P&L per approved trade: %s." % pct(np.mean([r["pnl_pct"] for r in approved]) if k else None),
        "Buy-and-hold over the split, mean across tickers: %s." % pct(bh_return), "",
        "Notes: no fees or slippage. Every plan uses the fixed +5%/-3%/10-day levels, so swarm",
        "outcomes and labels score the same bet. Break-even precision is 37.5%.",
        "Fewer than 50 approved trades: read as directional only.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="validation", choices=["train", "validation"])
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="only the first N setups (smoke run)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="JSONL path (default runs/swarm_<split>.jsonl)")
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1, help="setups decided in parallel")
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true",
                        help="keep finished setups from --out and re-decide only errors and missing ones")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", default="deepseek", choices=["deepseek", "claude"],
                        help="deepseek needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; claude needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from src.llm import make_llm
    from src.tools import load_market
    from src.tracing import make_tracer

    market = load_market()
    tracer = make_tracer(tags=("trading-swarm", "provider:" + args.provider))
    records = run(args.split, market, make_llm(tracer, args.provider), tracer, args.limit, args.out,
                  args.workers, args.resume)
    tracer.flush()
    summary = summarize(records, market, args.split, cost=tracer.total_cost())
    with open(SUMMARY_PATH, "w") as f:
        f.write(summary)
    print(summary)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                bt = backtest(plan, market, date)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = normalized(plan), bt
            with tracer.span("agent", "mathematician", agent="mathematician", round=rnd, **tags) as rec:
                math = mathematician.run(plan, bt)
                rec["input"], rec["output"] = bt, math
            verdict, objections = naysayer.run(llm, normalized(plan), facts, math, round=rnd, **tags)
            if verdict == "approve":
                break
    return {"ticker": ticker, "date": date, "split": setup["split"], "rounds": rnd,
            "verdict": "approve" if verdict == "approve" else "dropped",
            "plan": plan, "objections": objections}


def run(split, market, llm, tracer, limit=None, out_path=None, workers=1, resume=False):
    """Decide every setup in `split`, simulate approved trades, write JSONL. Returns the records.

    With workers > 1, setups are decided in parallel threads; lines are still written in
    setup order. With resume, setups already in out_path without an error are kept as they
    are and only the rest are decided. Output goes to a temp file that replaces out_path at
    the end, so an interrupted run never destroys earlier results.
    """
    if split == "test":
        raise SystemExit("The swarm step does not run on the test split.")
    rows = market.setups[market.setups["split"] == split]
    if limit:
        rows = rows.head(limit)
    out_path = out_path or os.path.join("runs", "swarm_%s.jsonl" % split)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)

    done = {}
    if resume and os.path.exists(out_path):
        with open(out_path) as f:
            for line in f:
                r = json.loads(line)
                if r["verdict"] != "error":
                    done[(r["ticker"], r["date"])] = r

    def one(setup):
        if (setup["ticker"], setup["date"]) in done:
            return done[(setup["ticker"], setup["date"])]
        try:
            rec = decide(setup, market, llm, tracer)
        except Exception as e:     # one bad setup must not stop the run; it is logged as an error
            rec = {"ticker": setup["ticker"], "date": setup["date"], "split": split,
                   "rounds": None, "verdict": "error", "plan": None, "objections": [],
                   "error": repr(e)}
        # The decision is fixed above. Only now does anything read prices after the setup date.
        if rec["verdict"] == "approve":
            rec.update(simulate(rec["plan"], market, setup["ticker"], setup["date"]))
        else:
            rec.update(trade_outcome=None, pnl_pct=None)
        rec["label"] = int(setup["label"])   # for scoring only; agents never saw it
        return rec

    records = []
    tmp_path = out_path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w") as f, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        for rec in pool.map(one, rows.to_dict("records")):   # map keeps setup order
            f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
            f.flush()
            records.append(rec)
    os.replace(tmp_path, out_path)
    return records


def summarize(records, market, split, cost=0.0, seed=0):
    """Markdown summary: swarm vs random approvals vs always-approve vs buy-and-hold."""
    labels = np.array([r["label"] for r in records])
    approved = [r for r in records if r["verdict"] == "approve"]
    n, k = len(records), len(approved)
    rate = k / n if n else 0.0
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    random_pick = rng.random(n) < rate                      # same approval rate as the swarm
    dates = market.setups.loc[market.setups["split"] == split, "date"]
    bh = [market.prices[t].loc[dates.min():dates.max(), "Adj Close"] for t in market.prices]
    bh_return = float(np.mean([s.iloc[-1] / s.iloc[0] - 1 for s in bh]))

    def pct(x):
        return "n/a" if x is None else "%.1f%%" % (100 * x)

    lines = [
        "# Swarm summary: %s split" % split, "",
        "| Item | Value |", "|---|---|",
        "| Setups | %d |" % n,
        "| Approved | %d (%s) |" % (k, pct(rate)),
        "| Dropped after %d rounds | %d |" % (MAX_ROUNDS, sum(r["verdict"] == "dropped" for r in records)),
        "| Errors | %d |" % sum(r["verdict"] == "error" for r in records),
        "| LLM cost | $%.4f |" % cost, "",
        "## Precision of approved trades (share that hit +5% before -3%)", "",
        "| Method | Approved | Precision |", "|---|---|---|",
        "| Swarm | %d | %s |" % (k, pct(np.mean([r["trade_outcome"] == "win" for r in approved]) if k else None)),
        "| Random, same approval rate (seed %d) | %d | %s |" % (seed, random_pick.sum(), pct(labels[random_pick].mean() if random_pick.any() else None)),
        "| Always approve (= base rate) | %d | %s |" % (n, pct(labels.mean() if n else None)), "",
        "Mean P&L per approved trade: %s." % pct(np.mean([r["pnl_pct"] for r in approved]) if k else None),
        "Buy-and-hold over the split, mean across tickers: %s." % pct(bh_return), "",
        "Notes: no fees or slippage. Every plan uses the fixed +5%/-3%/10-day levels, so swarm",
        "outcomes and labels score the same bet. Break-even precision is 37.5%.",
        "Fewer than 50 approved trades: read as directional only.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="validation", choices=["train", "validation"])
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="only the first N setups (smoke run)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="JSONL path (default runs/swarm_<split>.jsonl)")
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1, help="setups decided in parallel")
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true",
                        help="keep finished setups from --out and re-decide only errors and missing ones")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", default="deepseek", choices=["deepseek", "claude"],
                        help="deepseek needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; claude needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from src.llm import make_llm
    from src.tools import load_market
    from src.tracing import make_tracer

    market = load_market()
    tracer = make_tracer(tags=("trading-swarm", "provider:" + args.provider))
    records = run(args.split, market, make_llm(tracer, args.provider), tracer, args.limit, args.out,
                  args.workers, args.resume)
    tracer.flush()
    summary = summarize(records, market, args.split, cost=tracer.total_cost())
    with open(SUMMARY_PATH, "w") as f:
        f.write(summary)
    print(summary)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

cd "D:/user/projects/trading-swarm" && cat >> docs/SWARM_SPEC.md <<'EOF'

## 15. Cost controls (owner, 2026-10-11)

The validation run cost about $0.038 per setup (upper bound). The Planner made two thirds of the LLM calls (1,154 of ~1,760), all on `deepseek-v4-pro` with thinking on. Changes, decided by the owner after that run:

1. **Price watcher.** The swarm runs only when a setup shows an unusual 1-day move: `|ret_1d| >= 1.5 x vol_20d`, up or down. Other setups are logged with verdict `skipped`, rounds 0, and no LLM call. The 1.5 was chosen from trigger frequency alone (12.3% of train days, 17.0% of validation days), before looking at any outcome. Both features are known on the setup day, so the watcher adds no leakage.
2. **Second round only for fixable failures.** After a block, the Planner gets round 2 unless the gate's reason was break-even: at least 30 matches, not too broad, and the cautious hit rate still at or below 37.5%. Rewording does not change that evidence. Too few matches, too broad, invalid plans, and Naysayer objections still get round 2. In the first validation run, every setup used both rounds and round 2 produced one approval.
3. **Planner effort: unchanged.** The owner asked for medium. DeepSeek's OpenAI-format API accepts `low`, `high` and `max`, and maps `medium` to `high`, so medium costs the same as today. Open decision: keep `high`, or try `low`.
4. **Gate pre-check: evaluated, not built.** Idea: before calling the Planner, search simple theses (1 or 2 conditions at train deciles that the setup satisfies) in code, and skip the LLM if none passes the gate. Measured on the 98 triggered validation setups: every one has a passing single condition, so the pre-check would skip 0%.

**Finding for the gate (open, for the owners):** the pre-check result shows a loose single condition, e.g. `ret_1d` above its 30th percentile, matches about 70% of eligible setups, stays under the 80% "too broad" cap, and passes, because the train base rate (40.5%) is above the 37.5% break-even and the Wilson lower bound of a large sample sits just above it. The Planner did not write such theses in the first run, but nothing stops it. Options: lower the cap (e.g. 50%), or require the matched hit rate to beat the eligible base rate, not only break-even.

Tests added (section 11): a quiet setup is skipped with no LLM call; a 1.5-sigma move wakes the swarm; a break-even block ends after round 1; too-few and too-broad blocks get round 2.
EOF
tail -3 docs/SWARM_SPEC.md

input.command:
cd "D:/user/projects/trading-swarm" && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, collections
from src.tools import load_market, wilson_low
from src.features import FEATURE_NAMES
m = load_market(); s = m.setups
train = s[s.split == "train"].reset_index(drop=True); labels = train.label.to_numpy()
qs = np.round(np.arange(0.1, 1.0, 0.1), 1)
val = s[s.split == "validation"]
trig = val[(val.ret_1d.abs() / val.vol_20d) >= 1.5].to_dict("records")
shares, examples = [], collections.Counter()
for row in trig:
    known = (train.outcome_end < pd.Timestamp(row["date"])).to_numpy(); elig = known.sum()
    best = None
    for f in FEATURE_NAMES:
        for q, t in zip(qs, np.quantile(train[f], qs)):
            ge = row[f] >= t
            mask = ((train[f] >= t) if ge else (train[f] <= t)).to_numpy() & known
            n = mask.sum()
            if 30 <= n <= 0.8 * elig:
                low = wilson_low(int(labels[mask].sum()), int(n))
                if low > 0.375 and (best is None or n / elig < best[0]):
                    best = (n / elig, "%s %s p%d" % (f, ">=" if ge else "<=", round(q * 100)), low)
    shares.append(best[0]); examples[best[1]] += 1
print("narrowest passing single condition per setup: match share min %.0f%%, median %.0f%%, max %.0f%%" % (100*min(shares), 100*np.median(shares), 100*max(shares)))
print("most common narrowest passing conditions:", examples.most_common(5))
EOF

# Building the business plan in cfo.ai

The model is ready as an Excel workbook: `results/business_model.xlsx`. cfo.ai's assistant, Ari, can import a workbook and rebuild it as a native cfo.ai model, turning the assumptions into Variables and the two cases into Scenarios (cfo.ai docs: "Import a spreadsheet model").

## What's in the workbook

| Sheet | Contents |
|---|---|
| Summary | 24-month results for both scenarios: customers, MRR, gross margin, operating profit, lowest cash, runway, break-even, funding need, LTV:CAC |
| Assumptions | Every input with its source. Blue = input, yellow = owner estimate to confirm. Column B = Base, column C = Growth |
| Model_Base, Model_Growth | Monthly model: customers, revenue, payment fees, LLM and Laya cost, gross profit, marketing, fixed costs, operating profit, cash |
| Unit_Economics | One watchlist per month: contribution margin, CAC payback, LTV, LTV:CAC |

Every output is a formula; there are no typed-in results. All 1,010 formulas were evaluated (with pycel) and checked against an independent Python calculation of the same model; they match. The file has no cached values, because it was written by a script: Excel computes them when it opens the file, and Ari reads the formulas.

## Measured vs assumed

- **Measured:** LLM cost per decision, $0.038 (upper bound at DeepSeek peak prices, from the validation run in `results/README.md`).
- **Standard pricing:** card fees, 2.9% + $0.30 (Stripe US).
- **Owner estimates (yellow):** price ($19 per watchlist per month), new customers, growth, churn, CAC, hosting, neatlogs, team cost, starting cash. Change them before presenting the plan if you have better numbers.

## Results with the current assumptions

| | Base | Growth |
|---|---|---|
| Customers, month 24 | 238 | 1,504 |
| MRR, month 24 | $4,516 | $28,569 |
| Contribution margin per watchlist | $14.16 (74.5%) | $14.16 (74.5%) |
| LTV to CAC | 5.9x | 5.9x |
| Break-even month | 22 | 18 |
| Lowest cash balance | $682 | −$43,130 |
| Funding needed to never go below zero | $0 | $43,130 |

Reading: unit economics are healthy because inference is cheap per decision. Base survives on $25,000 but only just. Growth needs about $43,000 of outside funding before it breaks even in month 18.

## Steps (Zeeshan)

1. Sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks. **Cancel the subscription immediately** in Settings → Billing, as the hackathon page instructs. The neatHack team provides credits.
2. Optional: open `results/business_model.xlsx` in Excel, change any yellow assumption, and save. Saving in Excel also stores the computed values.
3. Start a conversation with Ari, attach the workbook, and paste:

   > Import this workbook into cfo.ai as a native Model. It is a 24-month plan for a subscription product priced per watchlist. Make every input on the Assumptions sheet a Variable. Make column B (Base) the Main scenario and column C (Growth) a second Scenario. Keep the monthly time grain starting at month 1, with no Actuals.

4. Check the rebuild, paste:

   > Reconcile the rebuilt revenue, gross profit, operating profit and ending cash to the attached workbook for months 12 and 24 in both scenarios, and list any differences.

5. Ask Ari for the runway view and a short plan summary:

   > Show runway and the funding needed for each scenario, and draft a one-page business plan summary from this Model.

6. Share the model or page as a read-only link and put the link, plus a screenshot, in the submission. Save a PDF or screenshots to `results/` too.

**Done when:** the Model has both Scenarios, the reconciliation shows no differences, and the share link is in the submission.

content.text:
The cost cuts work in a live run. This was a 30-setup smoke test with the watcher and the conditional retry (keys redacted in the output):

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Setups that call the LLM | 30 of 30 | **8 of 30** (22 skipped by the watcher, no LLM call) |
| Cost per setup that runs | $0.038 | **$0.025** (3 of 8 ended after round 1) |
| Cost per setup overall | $0.038 | **$0.0066**, about 83% cheaper |

All costs are upper bounds at DeepSeek peak prices. Zero errors.

**What I implemented**
- **7. Price watcher:** the swarm runs only on a 1-day move of at least 1.5× the 20-day volatility, up or down. That's about 12% of train days. I picked 1.5 from trigger frequency alone, before looking at any outcomes. Other days are logged as `skipped` with no LLM call.
- **5. Conditional round 2:** no retry when the gate says "enough evidence, and the bet loses" (break-even). Too few matches, too broad, invalid plans, and Naysayer objections still get round 2.
- 115 tests pass, including new ones for both changes. `docs/SWARM_SPEC.md` has a new section 15 recording all of this.

**Not implemented**
- **2. Gate pre-check:** I measured it first, and it would skip 0 of 98 setups. Every triggered setup has some narrow single condition that passes on train, most often "1-day return in the top 10%". So it saves nothing.
- **Correction to my last message:** I said loose conditions matching about 70% of setups could slip past the gate. When I checked the numbers, that was wrong: the passing conditions match 9–50% of setups (median 20%). The spec has the corrected finding.
- **3. Planner effort:** DeepSeek has no medium. It only accepts `low`, `high`, and `max`, and maps `medium` to `high`, so nothing changed. Want to try `low`?

**cfo.ai workbook updated:** a new watcher input (12.3% of days) feeds the model. The LLM cost per watchlist drops from $3.99 to $0.49 a month. Contribution margin is now **$17.66 (93%)**, LTV:CAC **7.4×**, and the Growth case needs **$28.5k** of funding instead of $43k. All formulas re-checked. I kept the per-decision cost at the conservative $0.038, since the $0.025 comes from only 8 setups.

**Uncommitted, waiting on your OK:** the watcher and retry code with its tests, spec section 15, `results/business_model.xlsx`, `docs/CFO_AI.md`, and the `docs/NEXT_STEPS.md` link. Should I commit and push them to `swarm`? A full validation re-run with the new setup would then cost roughly $2–3 at most and give fresh numbers for the demo and cfo.ai.

content.text: "Model" could mean the trading swarm or the business plan. Both are covered below, starting with the swarm. The swarm only outputs approve or drop, so its validation run says little directly. But for the 329 setups dropped as below break-even, the log records the Planner's thesis hit rate on train. Comparing those numbers against what actually happened on validation is a free test of whether the theses carry any signal:

input.command:
cd "D:/user/projects/trading-swarm" && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
import json, re, numpy as np
rs = [json.loads(l) for l in open("results/swarm_validation.jsonl")]
pat = re.compile(r"plain ([\d.]+)% over (\d+) setups")
xs, ys = [], []
for r in rs:
    m = pat.search(r["objections"][0]) if r["objections"] else None
    if m:
        xs.append(float(m.group(1)) / 100); ys.append(r["label"])
xs, ys = np.array(xs), np.array(ys)
def auc(x, y):
    pos, neg = x[y == 1], x[y == 0]
    return ((pos[:, None] > neg[None, :]).sum() + 0.5 * (pos[:, None] == neg[None, :]).sum()) / (len(pos) * len(neg))
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
boot = [auc(xs[i], ys[i]) for i in (rng.integers(0, len(xs), len(xs)) for _ in range(2000))]
print("setups with a thesis backtest: %d | actual win rate: %.1f%%" % (len(xs), 100 * ys.mean()))
print("thesis train hit rate (mean): %.1f%%" % (100 * xs.mean()))
print("AUC of thesis hit rate vs real outcome: %.3f (90%% interval %.3f-%.3f)" % (auc(xs, ys), *np.percentile(boot, [5, 95])))
hi = xs >= np.median(xs)
print("win rate when thesis hit rate above median: %.1f%%, below: %.1f%%" % (100 * ys[hi].mean(), 100 * ys[~hi].mean()))
EOF

content.text:
**As a trade picker, the swarm has no measurable skill.**

- **It approved 1 of 577 validation setups, and that trade lost 3%.** One trade can't tell you anything about precision.
- **Its theses carry no signal.** For the 322 setups where the Planner's thesis was backtested, I compared the thesis's train hit rate against what actually happened:
  - **AUC 0.45** (90% interval 0.40–0.50), where 0.5 is a coin flip.
  - When the thesis looked *better* on train (above-median hit rate), real outcomes were *worse*: a 32% win rate, against 38% below the median.
- **That matches Elena's ML baselines,** which got AUC 0.46–0.50 on the same features. The Planner produces sensible-sounding theses ("buy the dip in an uptrend"), but on this data they don't predict anything.
- **Why:** the only inputs are 7 features from daily prices of 5 mega-cap stocks. A +5%/−3% move over 10 days isn't predictable from that. That's the expected outcome for heavily traded stocks, not a bug.

**What it is good at**
- **Saying no when there's no edge.** Approving everything wins 36.6% of the time, below the 37.5% needed to break even, so the swarm was right to refuse. But a rule of "never trade" would score the same, so refusing alone isn't skill.
- **Engineering:** 577 decisions with 0 errors, no lookahead leakage, every step traced in neatlogs, and now about 83% cheaper to run.

**What could actually make it better**
1. **Better inputs.** News or earnings dates (open item 4 in Elena's handover), overall market direction (e.g. the S&P 500), volume. Prices alone are the weak point.
2. **More data:** more tickers and longer history, so real patterns have enough examples to show up.
3. **A different bet.** +5%/−3% in 10 days on mega-caps is a hard target.

Laya won't fix this. It learns from the same price features, so it can't find a signal that isn't there.

**The business model (cfo.ai workbook)** is solid on costs, which come from measured LLM spend: $0.49 per watchlist per month with the watcher. The revenue side (price, customer numbers, churn) is my placeholder estimate, so read it as a scenario plan, not a forecast. Its weak point is the same as the swarm's: the pitch "it refuses bad trades" currently does no better than never trading.

**For the hackathon,** the honest version is the strong one. Judges score verification, and "we measured it, found no signal, and the agent correctly refused to trade" is a well-supported story. If you'd rather aim for real skill, better inputs (option 1) are the way. That's a new piece of work, and it would need its own spec before the one-shot test run.

content.text:
Probably not, the way it's set up now.

**Why Laya won't help as-is:** Elena fine-tuned it on the same 7 price features the swarm and the ML baselines already use. Every method that has looked at those features, including the swarm's theses, lands at coin-flip, AUC 0.45–0.50. Laya can't extract information that isn't in its input. Its 0.69 accuracy was measured on its own training period, so it doesn't count yet. Elena's validation scoring (Kaggle, about 30 minutes) will settle it, and I expect around 0.5.

**Where Laya *could* help:** Laya is a fast, cheap **text** classifier. Its strength is reading words: news headlines, earnings announcements, company filings. Fed text, it could turn each day's news into features ("earnings beat", "lawsuit", "downgrade") for the swarm. That adds *new information*, which is the only thing that can create an edge. The catch is finding historical, timestamped news for 2024–2026 for free, which is hard.

**What I'd do to make it "a little good," cheapest first:**
1. **Test new inputs with plain ML before touching the agents.** Free (no LLM calls), about 30 minutes:
   - **Market direction:** S&P 500 / Nasdaq trend and the VIX fear index, free from Yahoo.
   - **Earnings timing:** days since the last earnings report. Big moves cluster around earnings, and "days since" uses only the past, so there's no leakage.
   - **Volume:** unusual trading volume.

   Re-run Elena's baselines with these added. If validation AUC rises clearly above 0.5, there's real signal to give the swarm.
2. **If there's signal,** add the features to the setup table. The Planner can then write theses like "after earnings, with the market trending up", and the gate tests them the same way. The existing code mostly handles it.
3. **Laya on text, only if 1 works and we find a historical news source:** use it to tag earnings and news events. That's the bigger, riskier step.
4. **Elena runs her Laya validation scoring anyway,** so the submission can say honestly what Laya added.

If step 1 finds nothing, we've lost 30 minutes and we know the honest story is the right one.

Should I start step 1 now?

"""SPIKE (throwaway): do market, earnings, or volume features add validation signal over the 7 price features?

Train on train, score on validation, same models and block bootstrap as src/baselines.py.
Feature groups were fixed before running. The test split is not touched.
"""
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yfinance as yf

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from src.baselines import block_bootstrap, models, scores
from src.data import TICKERS, load_prices
from src.features import FEATURE_NAMES
from src.labels import SETUPS_PATH

setups = pd.read_csv(SETUPS_PATH, parse_dates=["date"])
setups = setups[setups.split.isin(["train", "validation"])].reset_index(drop=True)

# ---- market: S&P 500 (SPY) and VIX, values at or before each setup day
mk = yf.download(["SPY", "^VIX"], start="2023-06-01", end="2026-10-01", auto_adjust=False, progress=False)["Adj Close"]
spy, vix = mk["SPY"].dropna(), mk["^VIX"].dropna()
spy_f = pd.DataFrame({
    "spy_ret_5d": spy / spy.shift(5) - 1,
    "spy_ret_20d": spy / spy.shift(20) - 1,
    "spy_close_to_ma50": spy / spy.rolling(50).mean(),
    "vix_level": vix.reindex(spy.index).ffill(),
    "vix_chg_5d": (vix / vix.shift(5) - 1).reindex(spy.index).ffill(),
})
spy_f.index = spy_f.index.tz_localize(None).normalize()

# ---- earnings: last report strictly before the setup date (most are after the close)
earn = {}
for t in TICKERS:
    e = yf.Ticker(t).get_earnings_dates(limit=24)
    e = e[e["Reported EPS"].notna()].copy()
    e.index = e.index.tz_convert("America/New_York").tz_localize(None).normalize()
    earn[t] = e.sort_index()

# ---- volume from the stored prices
vol = {t: load_prices(t)["Volume"] for t in TICKERS}

rows = []
for r in setups.itertuples():
    d = r.date
    out = {}
    m = spy_f.loc[:d].iloc[-1]
    out.update(m.to_dict())
    out["rel_ret_20d"] = r.ret_20d - m["spy_ret_20d"]
    e = earn[r.ticker]
    past = e[e.index < d]
    if len(past):
        last = past.index[-1]
        px = vol[r.ticker].index
        out["days_since_earnings"] = int(((px > last) & (px <= d)).sum())
        out["last_surprise_pct"] = float(np.clip(past["Surprise(%)"].iloc[-1], -50, 50))
    else:
        out["days_since_earnings"], out["last_surprise_pct"] = np.nan, np.nan
    v = vol[r.ticker].loc[:d]
    out["vol_ratio_20d"] = v.iloc[-1] / v.iloc[-21:-1].mean()
    out["vol_ratio_5d"] = v.iloc[-1] / v.iloc[-6:-1].mean()
    rows.append(out)
X = pd.concat([setups, pd.DataFrame(rows)], axis=1)

GROUPS = {
    "market": ["spy_ret_5d", "spy_ret_20d", "spy_close_to_ma50", "vix_level", "vix_chg_5d", "rel_ret_20d"],
    "earnings": ["days_since_earnings", "last_surprise_pct"],
    "volume": ["vol_ratio_20d", "vol_ratio_5d"],
}
SETS = {"price only (7)": list(FEATURE_NAMES)}
for g, cols in GROUPS.items():
    SETS["price + " + g] = list(FEATURE_NAMES) + cols
SETS["price + all (primary)"] = list(FEATURE_NAMES) + sum(GROUPS.values(), [])

print("missing values:", int(X[sum(GROUPS.values(), [])].isna().sum().sum()), "| setups:", X.split.value_counts().to_dict())
tr, va = X[X.split == "train"], X[X.split == "validation"]
y_tr, y_va = tr.label.to_numpy(), va.label.to_numpy()
print("\n| Features | Model | Validation AUC | 90% interval |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for name, cols in SETS.items():
    preds = {}
    for mname, model in models().items():
        if mname == "Base rate":
            continue
        model.fit(tr[cols].fillna(tr[cols].median()), y_tr)
        preds[mname] = model.predict_proba(va[cols].fillna(tr[cols].median()))[:, 1]
    ci = block_bootstrap(va.date.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), y_va, preds)
    for mname, p in preds.items():
        lo, hi = ci[mname]["auc"]
        print("| %s | %s | %.3f | %.3f-%.3f |" % (name, mname, scores(y_va, p)["auc"], lo, hi))
X.to_csv(sys.argv[1], index=False)

Also no signal: every model scores around 0.5 for predicting even near-term *risk* on this data.

That changes the diagnosis. The bigger problem isn't missing inputs. **The dataset is too small to show anything either way.** Validation is 123 trading days × 5 stocks, and neighboring days share the same future prices. So every interval spans about ±0.12 around the estimate, and validation also behaved very differently from train (a 3% drop followed 64% of validation days, against 51% of train days). Even a real, modest edge (AUC 0.55) would be invisible here.

**Where this leaves "make the agents do something":**

| Option | What it takes | Chance it works |
|---|---|---|

"""SPIKE (throwaway): with 50 stocks and train back to 2015, is there validation signal for the +5%/-3% bet?
